# Schema Fixtures

One SQL fixture per shipped schema version, used by `tests/test_schema_fixtures.py` to verify that every historical DB shape migrates cleanly to the current `SCHEMA_VERSION`.

## How to add a fixture when bumping SCHEMA_VERSION

After updating `SCHEMA_VERSION` in `src/siftd/storage/sqlite.py` and implementing the new migration:

1. Run `./dev gen-schema-fixture` to dump the current fully-migrated schema into `tests/fixtures/schemas/v<N>.sql`.
2. Commit the new fixture alongside your migration code.

Legacy fixtures (older versions) are frozen — never edit them after the fact. They represent the exact on-disk shape users would have had at that schema version.

## Why v0 and v2 are synthesized

No real user DB was captured at these versions. `v0_pre_versioning.sql` is derived from the current `schema.sql` by stripping `ON DELETE CASCADE`/`SET NULL` and the optional columns (`branch`, `error`, `file_mtime`, `file_size`) that were added by early unversioned migrations. `v2.sql` is generated by loading v0 into a temp DB, running the unversioned column migrations and `MIGRATIONS[2]` (cascade contract enforcement), and dumping the result. This gives confidence that both code paths exercise real migration logic rather than relying on hand-crafted SQL that might drift from the actual migration output.

From v3 onward, fixtures are true captures produced by running `./dev gen-schema-fixture`.
